MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L11·N83unmasked layer
This neuron's activation is driven by the opening token of highly predictable formulaic multi-word expressions — negative-contraction stems ("don"/"doesn"/"won" before "'t") and collocation heads like "same" in *at the same time*, "rest" in *rest of the*, "according" in *according to*, "to" in *extent to which* — with the largest-magnitude responses (negative) falling on the very same class of tokens, so it tracks fixed-idiom continuation slots rather than any topical content.

This neuron fires on short function words (in, the, that, to, she) immediately after a content word where they begin a new phrase/complement, and is suppressed when the same function words are part of a fixed collocation or idiomatic particle ("check in", "join in", "in vacation of", "cheer and") — so it appears to track whether a post-verb/noun function word starts a fresh phrase versus fusing with the preceding word.
